the Late Permion Zechstein cycle II was characterized by a complex interplay of oceanographic and climatic factors, which resulted in the development of a highly variable and complex palaeo-oceanographic setting, which in turn influenced the distribution of organic matter in the sediments.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of PZE does not necessarily imply widespread anoxia in the water column.
anoxic and euxinic conditions in the photic zones of the Late Permian seas were not ubiquitous, but rather were highly variable in both space and time.

the presence of organic matter with high concentrations of biomarkers for photic zone euxinic conditions (PZE) in the Zechstein 2 carbonates does not imply that these rocks are sourced from anoxic conditions, but instead are sourced from an oxygenated photic zone.
